pins.title: Qīngyáng 清扬 — the oldest compliment to a beautiful person
pins.description: Bright eyes, clear brow. This is the exact phrase the Book of Songs — China's oldest poetry, 3,000 years old — used to describe a beautiful person. A name that has meant graceful beauty since before Rome was founded. See the full meaning and origin: https://mychinesename.co/name/qingyang

pins.title: Wǎnxī 婉兮 — grace itself, from the oldest Chinese poetry
pins.description: Soft, graceful, unforgettable. 'Wǎnxī' comes from the Book of Songs, where a traveler falls in love at first sight on a morning of wild grass and dew. One of the most poetic two characters ever written for a girl. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/wanxi

pins.title: Jiāshù 嘉树 — the noble tree Qu Yuan praised
pins.description: Qu Yuan, China's first great poet, praised one tree above all: the orange tree — 'the noblest of all fine trees'. A name for someone you hope will stand tall and stay fragrant through every season. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/jiashu

pins.title: Yōulán 幽兰 — the orchid hidden in the deep valley
pins.description: Confucius said the orchid is 'the king of fragrances', yet it blooms quietly in empty valleys, asking no one's praise. 'Yōulán' is for quiet strength and hidden talent. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/youlan

pins.title: Jìngjiē 静姝 — 'a quiet, beautiful girl', straight from the Book of Songs
pins.description: Three thousand years ago, the Book of Songs described an ideal woman with exactly these two characters: still as still water, lovely beyond compare. The most timeless compliment in Chinese. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/jingjie

pins.title: Zhānlù 湛露 — heavy morning dew, fresh and radiant
pins.description: From the Book of Songs: 'the heavy dew of dawn'. Pure, luminous, full of morning promise. A rare name that sounds like first light on leaves. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/zhanlu

pins.title: Sùqīng 素卿 — pure, elegant, like white silk
pins.description: 'Sù' is un-dyed silk — purity without decoration. 'Qīng' is an intimate classical term of endearment. Together: understated elegance that needs no ornament. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/suqing

pins.title: Yáoyáo 夭夭 — 'peaches heavy on the branch', the Book of Songs' happiest name
pins.description: The most joyful line in the Book of Songs: 'peach tree young and tender, its blossoms bright'. 'Yáoyáo' means blooming, thriving, radiant with life. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/yaoyao

pins.title: Zhǐlán 芷兰 — angelica and orchid, the scholar's fragrance
pins.description: 'Zhǐ' is the fragrant angelica plant of the Chu ci; 'lán' the orchid Confucius loved. The classic pairing for a person of virtue and learning. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/zhilan

pins.title: Wēiyíng 微萦 — faintly lingering, like a melody you can't forget
pins.description: 'Wēi' — subtle, gentle. 'Yíng' — to linger, to curl around the heart. A modern-classical name for something beautiful that stays with you. Full story: https://mychinesename.co/name/weiying
